intro: Valley Forge, northwest of Philadelphia in Pennsylvania, is where the Continental Army spent the winter of 1777 to 1778, and the ground is now a national historical park. We map one tree here so far: an American sycamore at Pawling Farm whose long pale limbs lie along the grass and rise again, which a reader photographed and sent to us.
meta_description: An American sycamore at Pawling Farm, Valley Forge, whose limbs touch the ground and rise again, sent by a reader: where it is and how to find it.
question_meta: Valley Forge's mapped tree is a sprawling American sycamore at Pawling Farm, sent by a reader. Where it stands and what we know.
question_answer: The tree we map at Valley Forge is an American sycamore at Pawling Farm, off Pawlings Road in Valley Forge National Historical Park. A reader photographed it with a GPS fix. Its limbs spread over 42 metres by the reader's account, and some lie along the ground before rising again. The reader puts it at 260 to 285 years old.
question_context: A reader sent us this sycamore with a note that says what makes it worth the walk: "The boughs spread over 42 meters, some of which reach down, meld with the ground and then bend back up." Their photograph shows it. Long limbs of pale, mottled bark, white, grey and olive where the old bark has flaked, run out across the mown lawn of Pawling Farm, rest on the grass for metres and then turn upward into a wide green crown. Walking under it means stepping between branches. American sycamores grow big along rivers in the eastern United States, and Pawling Farm sits on the north side of the Schuylkill, inside Valley Forge National Historical Park. The reader gives its girth as 650 centimetres and its age as 260 to 285 years; those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen. If they are right, the tree was growing during the Continental Army's winter here in 1777 to 1778. If you know more about it, tell us on its page.

faq.q: Where is the sycamore at Valley Forge?
faq.a: At Pawling Farm, off Pawlings Road on the north side of the Schuylkill in Valley Forge National Historical Park. Our pin marks where its finder placed it.
A reader puts it at 260 to 285 years, and measured its girth at 695 centimetres in November 2026. Those are their figures; no register has measured it.

faq.q: Can I walk among the limbs?
faq.a: Yes, the farm lawn is part of the park. Step over the limbs, not on them: they are living branches.

trees.story:
"The boughs spread over 42 meters, some of which reach down, meld with the ground and then bend back up," wrote the reader who sent us this American sycamore from Pawling Farm in Valley Forge National Historical Park, and went back in November to photograph it bare.

The photographs show exactly that. Instead of holding its limbs up, the tree has let them down: long arms of pale, mottled bark, white and grey and olive where the old bark has flaked away, run out across the mown grass, lie along it for metres and then turn upward again into the crown, so that walking under the tree means stepping between its branches. Sycamores often grow this way when they have room and nobody prunes them.

The reader puts its age at 260 to 285 years, and on that November visit measured the trunk themselves: "Just shy of 7 meter circumference, 6.95 meters." Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen. If they are right, the tree was already growing when the Continental Army spent the winter of 1777 to 1778 at Valley Forge.

Pawling Farm lies off Pawlings Road on the north side of the Schuylkill. Walk all the way round and follow one limb from the trunk to where it rises again.

trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-17 reader judge: sent by a reader (c4b5f1b1-ce96-469b-805d-cf75390b7917, through the app). Photograph viewed: long pale mottled limbs of a sycamore snaking along the grass, touching down and rising again, under a green crown, a farm building and a second great trunk behind, daylight, colour. Published under the closed list for a reader's tree. The reader's own figures: name 'American Sycamore at Pawling Farm in Valley Forge National Park', species 'American Sycamore', age '260-285', girth 650 cm, note on 42 m spread. Every figure on the page is stated as theirs. 2026-11-17 reader judge (later): the same reader sent two more photographs (455f464a, fd777c00, bare, November) and wrote that the lead photograph from c4b5f1b1 was not one they took (report 1000077): it came off the page and fd777c00 leads. They measured the girth at 6.95 m that day (report 1000076, was 650 cm by their earlier estimate); stated in the story as theirs, girth_cm left empty (a reader's figure).
